cards.headline: 1 725 250 agricultural households (12.1 million people, 32 percent of the rural population) need emergency agricultural assistance across 34 provinces.

quote.text: A total of 1 725 250 agricultural households, representing 12.1 million people, corresponding to 32 percent of the rural population, are in need of emergency agricultural assistance across 34 provinces.

cards.headline: The likelihood of being AgHiN is highest among small livestock producers (35 percent), small and medium rainfed farmers (35 percent) and small irrigated farmers (31 percent); 40 percent of AgHiN are irrigated farmers.

quote.text: is higher among small livestock producers (35 percent of them are classified as in need), small and medium rainfed farmers (35 percent), and small irrigated farmers (31 percent)

cards.headline: The share of households affected by drought rose from 27 percent in September 2024 to 75 percent in September 2025, nearly threefold; drought was the shock crop producers reported most often.

quote.text: The proportion of households affected by drought rose dramatically from27 percent in September 2024 to75 percent in September 2025, nearly a threefold increase.

cards.headline: Provide assistance for spring wheat planting by the first week of April and for rainfed wheat by the end of March, depending on the local calendar and irrigation.

quote.text: Assistance for spring wheat planting should be provided by the first week of April and assistance for rainfed wheat should be provided by the end of March, depending on the local calendar and availability of irrigation

cards.headline: 90 percent of assisted households were satisfied with the assistance, and 59 percent of farmers supported by FAO reported expanding their planted area.

quote.text: Overall satisfaction with assistance was high and 90 percent of households indicated that they were satisfied.

context.population: people in agricultural households in need of agricultural livelihood support only

cards.headline: Of these, 6.4 million people (912 129 households, 17 percent of the rural population) need emergency agricultural livelihood support only, to produce food and protect their livelihoods.

quote.text: a total of 6.4 million people (912 129 households, corresponding to 17 percent of the rural population) need emergency agricultural livelihood support to enable them to produce food and protect their livelihoods

cards.headline: A logistic model found wealth characteristics and crop diversification, not drought exposure, to be significant predictors of being AgHiN; the AgHiN share is higher among the least well-off.

quote.text: has characteristics linked to wealth (source of drinking water, land size and livestock category) and crop diversification as significant factors, while being affected by drought was not

cards.headline: Both the 2025 winter wheat crop and the spring wheat crop are estimated below average because of low cumulative precipitation since October 2024.

quote.text: both the 2025 winter wheat crop (accounting for the bulk of annual production, finalized in June 2025) and the spring wheat crop (harvested in September 2025) are estimated at a below-average level due to low cumulative precipitation starting in October 2024

cards.headline: An estimated 793 340 agricultural households (4 029 280 people), 2 percent of the total agricultural population, need emergency agricultural assistance across the eight divisions.

quote.text: An estimated 793 340 agricultural households (4 029 280 people) representing2 percent of the total agricultural population are in need of emergency agricultural assistance across eight divisions of Bangladesh.

cards.headline: The AgHiN are concentrated in Rangpur (19 percent of AgHiN) and Chattogram (18 percent) divisions, and more than half are in the Barind and Coastal area hotspots.

quote.text: The AgHiN were found to be concentrated in Rangpur (19 percent) and Chattogram (18 percent) divisions.

cards.headline: AgHiN are asset-poor (including in education), almost all have less than half a hectare of often marginal, rainfed land and fewer animals; fisherfolk are more common among them.

quote.text: They are more likely asset-poor, including in education

cards.headline: 43 percent of AgHiN reported a decline in their main income compared with a year earlier, against a general rise in agricultural incomes.

quote.text: a significant proportion of the AgHiN (43 percent) reported a decline in their main income compared to the same period the previous year

cards.headline: 36 percent of AgHiN were denied loans, three times the share of households not in need; access to credit is a major barrier.

quote.text: Access to credit remains a major barrier – 36 percent of the AgHiN were denied loans, three times the share of those not in need of agricultural assistance.

cards.headline: Distribute crop inputs for the next Boro season (high-irrigated areas) between late November and January.

quote.text: Crop input interventions that target the next Boro season (high-irrigated areas) should prioritize the distribution of inputs between late November and January.

cards.headline: About 80 percent of assisted households were satisfied, but crop production assistance greatly decreased since the previous round and livestock assistance was delivered on a much smaller scale, suggesting coverage gaps.

quote.text: Although approximately 80 percent of households reported positive satisfaction with the assistance that they had received

cards.headline: Cox's Bazar (Chattogram) and Kurigram (Rangpur) districts have the highest proportion of AgHiN, around 9 percent of the district population.

quote.text: The districts of Cox’s Bazar in Chattogram division, and Kurigram in Rangpur have a particularly high proportion of AgHiN, estimated at around 9 percent of the total districts’ populations.

cards.headline: About 1 million agricultural households (about 5 million people) need emergency agricultural assistance from June to November 2026, up from 800 000 households in the September 2025 round (an increase of 200 000).

quote.text: approximately 1 million agricultural households – representing about 5 million people – are estimated to need emergency agricultural assistance from June to November 2026. This represents an increase compared to the September 2025 DIEM-Monitoring round, which found that 800 000 households were in need of emergency agricultural assistance.

cards.headline: Dhaka division had the largest increase in the number of AgHiN, from 50 000 to 157 000 households.

quote.text: Dhaka registered the largest increase in the number of AgHiN, up from 50 000 to 157 000 households.

cards.headline: 57 percent of AgHiN cultivated less than one hectare, against 35 percent of all agricultural households.

quote.text: Fifty-seven percent cultivated less than one hectare, compared with 35 percent of all agricultural households, a highly significant difference of 22 percentage points

cards.headline: Economic shocks affected 84 percent of AgHiN (similar to round 13) while exposure to natural hazards rose from 10 to 16 percent; agricultural shocks were broadly similar (24 and 22 percent).

quote.text: Agricultural-shock exposure also remained broadly similar, reported by 24 percent in the thirteenth round and 22 percent in the fourteenth round. In contrast, exposure to natural hazards rose by 6 percentage points, from 10 percent to 16 percent.

cards.headline: The share of AgHiN requesting cash assistance rose from 16 percent in round 13 to 57 percent.

quote.text: The share requesting cash assistance rose by an alarming 41 percentage points, from 16 percent in the thirteenth round to 57 percent in the fourteenth round

cards.headline: AgHiN prevalence rose most in the river-system and the Haor and flash-flood hotspot areas, reflecting exposure to flooding and waterlogging as the monsoon intensified.

quote.text: In terms of the hotspot areas, the AgHiN prevalence in river-system, and Haor and the flash-flood area had the biggest increase compared with the thirteenth round

cards.headline: 60 percent of AgHiN were in the lowest wealth tercile, against 33 percent of all agricultural households.

quote.text: Sixty percent of the AgHiN wereclassified in this tercile, compared with 33 percent of allagricultural households.

cards.headline: Crop sales difficulties among AgHiN crop producers rose from 9 percent to 30 percent; low selling prices were the main constraint.

quote.text: Crop-sales difficulties increased by 21 percentage points, from 9 percent in the thirteenth round to 30 percent in the fourteenth. Low selling prices were the main constraint reported by all of the crop producers who faced sales difficulties.

context.geography: eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo

cards.headline: In 2025, conflicts affected about half of the agricultural households in need, whether displaced people, returnees or host communities.

quote.text: En 2025, les conflits ont touché environ la moitié des ménages agricoles dans le besoin, qu'il s’agisse de personnes déplacées, de migrants de retour ou de communautés d'accueil.

cards.headline: 908 388 agricultural households (6 925 303 people, 27 percent of the total population of the four surveyed eastern provinces) need emergency agricultural assistance.

quote.text: Selon les estimations DIEM, 908 388 ménagesagricoles–soit 6 925 303 personnes,représentant 27 pour cent de la population totale des quatre provinces couvertes par l’enquête dans l’est du pays –nécessitent une assistance agricole d’urgence.

cards.headline: Agricultural households in need are concentrated mainly in Nord-Kivu (319 584 households), especially in Masisi and Rutshuru territories, although both territories, as well as Goma and Nyiragongo, improved compared with round 9.

quote.text: Les ménages agricoles dans le besoin se concentrent principalement au Nord-Kivu (319 584 ménages), en particulier dans les territoires de Masisiet Rutshuru

context.period: six months before the June-July 2025 survey

cards.headline: 51 percent of the agricultural population was displaced in the six months before the survey, above the general population (39 percent); this is down from 56 percent in round 9, reflecting many agricultural households returning to harvest.

quote.text: La part de la population agricole déplacée (51 pour cent) demeure supérieure à celle de la population générale déplacée (39 pour cent)

cards.headline: Since February 2025 the situation has been stabilizing, with fewer households affected by the conflict (45 percent against 61 percent in round 9), but volatility persists, notably in Nord-Kivu and Sud-Kivu.

quote.text: Depuis février 2025, la situation globale se stabilise, avec moins de ménages affectés par le conflit (45 pour cent contre 61 pour cent au cycle 9), mais la volatilité persiste, notamment au Nord-Kivu et au Sud-Kivu

cards.headline: Combine cash transfers and distribution of agricultural inputs to meet rising needs during the lean season; this assistance should run from October 2025, just before the rainy season, to February 2026 at harvest.

quote.text: Une assistance associant transferts monétaires et distribution d’intrants agricoles permettrait de répondre à l’augmentation des besoins durant cette période critique. Cette assistance devrait s’étendre d’octobre 2025, juste avant la saison des pluies, jusqu’à février 2026, au moment des récoltes.

context.period: three months before the June-July 2025 survey

cards.headline: Only 5 percent of the population reportedly received assistance in the three months before the survey, mainly food aid and cash transfers to displaced people; satisfaction with assistance received (77 percent) rose 5 points from round 9.

quote.text: Seuls 5 pour cent de la population auraient reçu une assistance au cours des trois mois précédant l’enquête.

cards.headline: In Kalehe territory (Sud-Kivu) the situation worsened slightly: 47 percent of agricultural households were in need, against 40 percent in round 9.

quote.text: Dans le territoire de Kalehe, la situation se détériore légèrement, avec 47 pour cent des ménages agricoles classifiés comme étant dans le besoin, contre 40 pour cent au cycle 9.

context.geography: Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu and Tanganyika

cards.headline: 867 477 agricultural households (6 592 825 people, 25 percent of the total population of the four eastern provinces) require emergency agricultural assistance.

quote.text: or 867 477 agricultural households, representing 25 percent of the total population, require emergency agricultural assistance.

cards.headline: The number of AgHiN has decreased steadily since the July 2024 peak (round 8), from 1 129 895 to 867 477 in March 2026, though levels remain high.

quote.text: The number fell from 1 129 895 to 867 477 in the eleventh round conducted in March 2026 across the four provinces covered by the survey

context.population: small-scale producers with plots under 0.4 hectares

cards.headline: 47 percent of small-scale producers with plots smaller than 0.4 hectares are AgHiN, reaching 60 percent in South Kivu; in the most conflict-affected areas farm size matters less.

quote.text: Forty-seven percent of small-scale producers with plots smaller than 0.4 hectares are classified as needing assistance, reaching 60 percent in South Kivu

cards.headline: The share of households reporting violence and conflict as their main shock rose from 8 to 22 percent between January 2024 and January 2025, and reached 44 percent in January 2026.

quote.text: the proportion of households reporting violence and conflict as their main shock has increased sharply from 8 to 22 percent between January 2024 and January 2025, and reached 44 percent in January 2026

cards.headline: AgHiN needs focus on agricultural livelihood support (527 773 households) and cash assistance (477 546 households); food assistance is less frequent (126 478 households).

quote.text: the needs of agricultural households are primarily focused on agricultural livelihood support (527 773 households) and cash assistance (477 546 households). The need for food assistance was less frequent (126 478 households)

cards.headline: The March-May lean season (low stocks, high input demand) justifies integrated and anticipatory assistance combining cash transfers and agricultural input support, deployed immediately and maintained until the main harvests (June-August).

quote.text: The lean season (March–May), characterized by low stock and high demand for inputs, increases needs and justifies integrated and anticipatory assistance through the end of the harvest period (June–August).

context.period: three months before the January-March 2026 survey

cards.headline: Only 5 percent of the population reported receiving assistance in the three months before the survey; virtually no agricultural livelihood support was provided, a mismatch with the expressed needs.

quote.text: Only 5 percent of the population reported receiving assistance over the three months preceding the survey, highlighting the limited coverage of interventions.

cards.headline: The decrease is particularly evident in North Kivu (from 368 487 to 263 078 AgHiN) and Tanganyika (from 173 179 to 97 637 AgHiN).

quote.text: The decrease is particularly evident in North Kivu (from 368 487 to 263 078 AgHiN) and Tanganyika (from 173 179 to 97 637 AgHiN).

cards.headline: A little over 100 000 agricultural households in the rural areas of the surveyed departments need emergency assistance to support their food and income needs.

quote.text: In the rural areas of the surveyed departments, a little over 100 000 agricultural households are in need of emergency assistance to support their food and income needs.

cards.headline: Over half of the AgHiN are in three departments: Cordoba (30 000), Choco (20 000) and Magdalena (12 000).

quote.text: Out of the more than 100 000 households in need of emergency agricultural assistance, 30 000 are located in Córdoba, 20 000 in Chocó and 12 000 in Magdalena.

cards.headline: A little over 12 percent of AgHiN have food consumption scores indicative of crisis food insecurity or worse.

quote.text: According to the food consumption score, a little over 12 percent of the AgHiN are indicative of crisis food insecurity or worse.

context.population: rural agricultural households self-identifying as Afro-Colombian

cards.headline: About 40 percent of rural agricultural households that self-identify as Afro-Colombian are in need of emergency assistance, against 18 percent of the overall rural agricultural population.

quote.text: Among rural households involved in agriculture, about 40 percent of those that self-identify as Afro-Colombians are in need of emergency assistance

cards.headline: AgHiN are mainly affected by loss of employment, high food prices and floods; loss of employment and floods are more strongly associated with need for assistance than other shocks.

quote.text: The AgHiN tend to be impacted by certain shocks such as loss of employment, high food prices or floods.

cards.headline: In Choco and Cordoba needs are roughly equally split between agricultural and non-agricultural, while in Magdalena agricultural needs are much lower and focused mostly on food, indicating a more urgent situation there.

quote.text: In Chocó and Córdoba, the needs are more or less equally distributed between agricultural and non-agricultural needs, and in Magdalena the prevalence of agricultural needs is significantly lower and focused mostly on food

cards.headline: Deliver assistance such as agricultural inputs, cash or vouchers from January to April 2026 to ensure a good start to the main season, which begins between February and April 2026 depending on crop and location.

quote.text: In order to ensure a good start to the season for agricultural households, assistance such as agricultural inputs, cash or vouchers should be implemented at the beginning of 2026, from January to April.

cards.headline: 18 percent of the overall rural population involved in agriculture is in need of assistance.

quote.text: 18 percent of the overall rural population involved in agriculture is in need of assistance

cards.headline: 150 839 agricultural households in need (AgHiN) require emergency food assistance nationally in the first half of 2026.

quote.text: A nivel nacional, 150839 AgHiN requieren asistencia alimentaria de emergencia

cards.headline: Cortés, hit mainly by floods and heavy rain, holds the largest single share of AgHiN: 17 percent (25 884 households).

quote.text: La mayoría de los AgHiN (17 %) se encuentra en Cortés (25 884 hogares)

cards.headline: 51 percent of AgHiN earn income from casual agricultural labour; for 46 percent of them it is the main income source.

quote.text: El 51 % de los AgHiN obtiene ingresos a partir de trabajo agrícola ocasional. Dentro de este grupo, el 46 % reporta que esta es su principal fuente de ingresos

cards.headline: 57 percent of livestock producers in need had production difficulties, mostly animal disease or death; marketing problems were minimal.

quote.text: afectaron al 57 % de los productores pecuarias que necesitan asistencia de emergencia. La dificultad de producción más reportada fue la enfermedad o la muerte del ganado.

cards.headline: 83 percent of AgHiN need food; 42 percent report agricultural livelihood needs, led by agricultural inputs (64 percent of those) and vouchers (32 percent).

quote.text: El 83 % de la población de los AgHiNexpresó necesidad de alimentos, mientras que el 42 % reportó necesidades relacionadas con los medios de vida agrícolas

cards.headline: AgHiN are 6 percent of the total population and 16 percent of the agricultural population in the surveyed area.

quote.text: Esto representa el 6% de la población total y el 16% de la población agrícola en el área encuestada.

cards.headline: 44 percent of AgHiN (about 65 700 households) live in drought-affected dry-corridor departments; Santa Barbara, Choluteca and Lempira have the largest numbers there.

quote.text: El 44% (65700 hogares) se ubica en el corredor seco

context.population: AgHiN with day labour as main income

cards.headline: AgHiN whose main income is day labour earn on average L 267 per day, against L 467 for other agricultural households relying on day labour.

quote.text: Los AgHiN reciben, en promedio, L 267 por día de trabajo agrícola ocasional

context.geography: Lebanon (7 of 8 governorates surveyed, Beirut excluded)

cards.headline: About 6 percent of agricultural households (approximately 10 000 households) were classified as AgHiN, in need of emergency food security assistance.

quote.text: Around 6 percent of all agricultural households (approximately 10 000 households) were classified as in need of emergency food security assistance.

cards.headline: A much larger share, 32 percent of agricultural households (around 54 000 households), was classified as at risk of falling into the AgHiN category if exposed to further shocks.

quote.text: a substantially larger share (32 percent, or around 54 000 households) is classified as at risk

cards.headline: Akkar stands out, with around half of its agricultural households classified as AgHiN or at risk, against around four in ten in four other governorates.

quote.text: However, Akkar stands out, with around half of the agricultural households classified as AgHiN or at risk (Figure 1), significantly higher than other governorates.

cards.headline: Food consumption was stable, but almost three-quarters of agricultural households used crisis-level livelihood coping, mainly reducing agricultural input expenditure (72 percent) and health expenditure (52 percent).

quote.text: almostthree-quarters engaged in crisis level coping mechanismsto meet food consumption needs.

context.period: three months preceding the December 2025 survey

cards.headline: Only about one-third of agricultural households relied mainly on agriculture for income; the AgHiN depended more on low-skilled farm and off-farm daily wage labour (18 percent).

quote.text: The AgHiN were more dependent on low-skilled income sources such as farm and off-farm daily wage activities (18 percent)

context.period: three months preceding the December 2025 survey

cards.headline: Rising food prices were the most widespread shock (57 percent of the AgHiN, 63 percent of at-risk households, 43 percent overall); drought affected around 37 percent across all groups.

quote.text: The most widespread shock was rising food prices, affecting 57 percent of the AgHiN, 63 percent of at-risk households and 43 percent overall

context.period: six months following the December 2025 survey

cards.headline: Food assistance needs rose sharply with vulnerability: 73 percent of the AgHiN against 52 percent of at-risk households.

quote.text: Food-related needs increased sharply with vulnerability (52 percent of at-risk households and 73 percent of the AgHiN).

cards.headline: The AgHiN were more dependent on rainfed agriculture (74 percent) than at-risk households (59 percent).

quote.text: A larger percentage of the AgHiN (74 percent) were dependent on rainfed agriculture compared with at-risk households (59 percent).

cards.headline: In relative terms the AgHiN share is highest in the north: 17 percent of the agricultural population in Gao and 11 percent in Tombouctou.

quote.text: However, in relative terms, the proportion of AgHiN is particularly high in the north of the country (17 percent in Gao and 11 percent in Tombouctou).

cards.headline: Female-headed agricultural households are more likely to be in need and more often resort to crisis and emergency coping strategies (43 percent against 17 percent of male-headed households).

quote.text: Female-headed agricultural households are more likely to be in need and more frequently resort to crisis and emergency coping strategies (43 percent compared to 17 percent for male-headed households)

context.period: three months before the October-November 2025 survey

cards.headline: With food and fuel prices rising together, 52 percent of AgHiN reported lower income in the three months before the survey compared with the same period of the previous year.

quote.text: 52 percent of the AgHiN reporteda decrease in income over the three months preceding the survey compared with the same period of the previous year.

cards.headline: The two main needs of AgHiN are support for agricultural livelihoods (66 percent) and food assistance (63 percent); as a single priority, 40 percent chose food assistance and 33 percent support for agricultural activities.

quote.text: The two main needs5 expressed by the AgHiN are support for agricultural livelihoods (66 percent) and food assistance (63 percent). In terms of priorities,6 the requested food assistance (40 percent), and support for agricultural activities (33 percent)

cards.headline: Emergency agricultural needs have a dual nature: regions with chronic food insecurity (Gao, Ménaka, Tombouctou) and regions where insecurity has recently worsened living conditions (Kayes, Mopti, Ségou).

quote.text: There are regions experiencing chronic food insecurity (Gao, Ménaka and Tombouctou), and regions where insecurity has recently worsened living conditions (Kayes, Mopti and Ségou)

cards.headline: Rice producers are more likely to be in need than maize, millet or sorghum growers; for livestock producers, herd size has no significant effect on being in need, suggesting animal health matters more than quantity.

quote.text: Rice producers are more likely to be in need than those growing maize, millet or sorghum.

cards.headline: 53 percent of AgHiN were exposed to conflict and insecurity in the year before the survey; 21 percent of the agricultural population was affected by insecurity.

quote.text: Among all of the AgHiN, 53 percent were exposed to conflict and insecurity over the year preceding the survey.

context.period: 2025 season compared with the previous year

cards.headline: Although national cereal production was comparable to the previous year, 38 percent of AgHiN reported a reduced cultivated area and 47 percent a marked decrease in production compared with the previous year.

quote.text: Among the AgHiN, 38 percent reported a reduction in cultivated area and 47 percent reported a marked decrease in their production compared to the previous year.

cards.headline: 735 567 agricultural households (5.1 million people) require emergency food security and agricultural livelihood assistance in Malawi.

quote.text: A total of 735 567 agricultural households (representing 5.1 million people) require emergency food security and agricultural livelihood assistance in Malawi.

cards.headline: 75 percent of livestock producers in need faced production difficulties; those facing theft were more likely to be in need.

quote.text: Among livestock producers in need, 75 percent faced production difficulties. Livestock households that experienced production difficulties, in particular theft, were more likely to be in need.

cards.headline: Difficulty accessing fertilizer rose from 43 to 56 percent since December 2024, and difficulty accessing quality seeds from 11 to 19 percent.

quote.text: Access to quality seeds has become more problematic – increasing from 11 percent to 19 percent since December 2024 – and difficulty accessing fertilizer has grown significantly – increasing from 43 percent to 56 percent.

cards.headline: 88 percent of agricultural households faced crop production difficulties, mainly lack of access to fertilizer (56 percent) and irrigation (54 percent), then pests (37 percent) and plant disease (32 percent).

quote.text: Nearly all (88 percent) agricultural households faced crop production difficulties. The main issue reported was lack of access to fertilizer (56 percent) and irrigation (54 percent). Pest outbreaks (37 percent) and plant disease (32 percent)

cards.headline: Provide agricultural assistance (inputs, including cash transfers) during the rainy and lean season peak, from December 2025 to April 2026.

quote.text: It is in this critical period that agricultural assistance, such as inputs, including cash transfers, would help meet the needs of the households. This assistance is needed from December 2025 to April 2026

cards.headline: Only 3.8 percent of respondents received any assistance in the six months before the survey (2.1 percent food, 1.4 percent cash); 74 percent of recipients were satisfied, 15 percent found the quantity insufficient.

quote.text: Over the six months preceding the survey, only 3.8 percent of the respondents reported receiving any form of assistance. This included 2.1 percent who received food support, 1.4 percent who received cash

cards.headline: Of these, 437 262 agricultural households (3.1 million people) require emergency agricultural livelihood assistance.

quote.text: Out of these, 437 262 agricultural households (or 3.1 million people) require emergency agricultural livelihood assistance.

cards.headline: Households with electricity, private piped water and incomes in the top two quintiles (more than USD 400 over six months) were less likely to be AgHiN; households relying on casual farm labour were significantly more likely to be in need.

quote.text: Agricultural households that had access to electricity and clean drinking water from private piped water taps were less likely to be in need

context.geography: Niger, excluding the urban community of Niamey

cards.headline: AgHiN are 10 percent of the agricultural population and 9 percent of the total population in the areas covered.

quote.text: They represent 10 percent of the agricultural population and 9 percent of the total population in the areas covered

cards.headline: 59 percent of AgHiN households adopt emergency livelihood coping strategies and a further 28 percent crisis strategies (87 percent combined, a sum not printed in the brief).

quote.text: Twenty-eight percent of households adopt crisis coping strategies and 59 percent adopt emergency coping strategies

cards.headline: Economic shocks are the main driver: 51 percent of AgHiN reported one against 13 percent of the agricultural population; rising food prices were the most cited (27 percent).

quote.text: More than half of the AgHiN (51 percent) reported an economic shock, compared with 13 percent of the total agricultural population

cards.headline: Provide food and cash assistance during the lean season (June-September) to prevent erosion of productive assets.

quote.text: Food and cash assistance remain priorities during the lean season (June–September) to prevent the erosion of productive assets.

cards.headline: 91 percent of AgHiN received no assistance in the reference period; only 1 percent received agricultural livelihood support, against 60 percent needing it. Satisfaction among recipients is high (96 percent), so coverage is the main gap.

quote.text: the vast majority of the AgHiN (91 percent) reported not receiving any assistance during the reference period.

cards.headline: 28 percent of AgHiN households adopt crisis livelihood coping strategies (in addition to 59 percent emergency).

quote.text: Twenty-eight percent of households adopt crisis coping strategies and 59 percent adopt emergency coping strategies

cards.headline: 36 percent of AgHiN reported a shock directly affecting production (18 percent of the agricultural population), mainly plant and animal diseases and pests; 24 percent reported a natural shock, mainly drought (13 percent).

quote.text: More than a third (36 percent) reported a shock directly affecting their production, compared with 18 percent in the overall agricultural population.

cards.headline: Distribute crop inputs (seeds, fertilizer) and agricultural financial support between April and June, before the rainy season.

quote.text: Interventions such as the distribution of inputs, financial assistance for agricultural activities or supporting veterinary services are more effective when implemented between April and June, before the full onset of the rainy season.

cards.headline: An estimated 1 003 982 agricultural households (9 209 144 people) in northeast and northwest Nigeria, 25 percent of the agricultural population, need emergency agricultural assistance.

quote.text: An estimated 1 003 982 agricultural households across the northeast and northwest of Nigeria (9 209 144 people), representing four percent of the total population and 25 percent of the agricultural population, are in need of emergency agricultural assistance.

cards.headline: Most AgHiN are in the northeast: 28 percent of the agricultural population is AgHiN in Borno and 26 percent in Yobe, where conflict is a chronic issue.

quote.text: While AgHiN are spread across the northeast and northwest of Nigeria, the majority are in the northeast. Twenty-eight percent of the total agricultural population is classified as AgHiN in Borno and 26 percent in Yobe.

cards.headline: Returnee households are more likely to need emergency assistance than permanent residents: 90 percent of returnees are engaged in agriculture and 34 percent of them are AgHiN.

quote.text: returnee households have a higher probability of needing emergency assistance than permanent households, 90 percent of returnees are engaged in agriculture, and 34 percent of them are AgHiN.

context.period: three months before the September 2025 survey

cards.headline: 54 percent of the AgHiN reported income losses over the three months before the survey compared with the same period a year earlier.

quote.text: 54 percent of AgHiN reporting income losses over the three months preceding the survey compared to the same period the year before.

cards.headline: Crop inputs (seeds, fertilizer, pesticides) are the most requested support (over 80 percent); about 74 percent reported a need for cash and 72 percent for food, and about one-third for crop infrastructure.

quote.text: crop inputs (seeds, fertilizer, pesticides) stand out as the most requested form of support, with over 80 percent of all households expressing this need. Cash and food assistance also emerge as significant priorities – particularly among vulnerable households – where around 74 percent reported a need for cash and 72 percent a need for food.
